name: Training the Beast
summary: In Dun Morogh, Training the Beast brings young dwarven hunters to the end of their first trials. After learning to soothe and tame wild predators in the snowy crags, they travel to Ironforge to learn how to care for, train, and sustain an animal companion.

sections.title: From the Wild to the Forge
sections.body: After taming large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod, young hunters finish their trial near Kharanos under Grif Wildheart’s watch. Taming a beast is only half the bond. Grif sends his pupils up the mountain pass to Ironforge, where they seek the Hall of Arms in the military district.

sections.title: Belia Thundergranite's Teachings
sections.body: Belia Thundergranite teaches animal care in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms. Revered among the dwarven kingdom’s master animal trainers, she shows young hunters how to nourish and care for their pets, teach them new battlefield skills, and call their spirits back if they fall while defending their master. Her lessons help turn a frightened wild beast into a loyal partner.

sections.title: The Dwarven Hunter's Bond
sections.body: Dwarven tradition calls for respect between hunter and beast, not subjugation. Belia reminds young hunters that an animal companion reflects the care it receives. Fed well, respected, and properly trained, a beast will fight loyally against troggs, frost trolls, and any threat to Khaz Modan.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: Training the Beast completes a dwarf hunter’s foundational training. You learn how to care for a lasting animal companion, feed and train it, call it to your side, and bring it back if it dies.

Belia Thundergranite is a revered master animal trainer and senior instructor in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms. She teaches dwarf hunters care, discipline, and commands that help turn tamed beasts into lifelong allies.

faq.q: Where do I find Belia Thundergranite?
aliases: where is hall of arms ironforge
faq.answer: Belia Thundergranite is in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms, the city’s military wing. Dwarf and gnome warriors, hunters, and paladins gather and train there.

faq.q: What beasts do dwarven hunters tame before receiving this training?
faq.answer: Before this training, young hunters use a taming rod to soothe a large crag boar, a snow leopard, and an ice claw bear in Dun Morogh. Grif Wildheart oversees these trials.

faq.q: Why must dwarven hunters feed their pets?
faq.answer: Dwarven beast lore treats animal companions as partners, not tools. Neglecting a pet’s hunger worsens its mood and weakens its willingness to fight. Keeping it well-fed earns fierce loyalty and helps it fight at its best.
Grif Wildheart is a veteran hunter trainer beside the road east of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. He gives this training after you complete your third taming trial.

angles.text: As a hunter, you learn to feed, command, and revive a lasting animal companion.
As a dwarf, you inherit Khaz Modan’s tradition of treating bears, boars, and mountain cats as partners in exploring and defending the mountainous wilderness.
As an Alliance member, you rely on Ironforge’s beastmasters, who contribute heavily to Alliance scouting forces with loyal companions that patrol the frigid mountain passes.
